newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- President Farooq Leghari has announced a wide-ranging economic reforms programme focusing on a relief package for the poor and measures to wipe out corruption.

- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said that President Farooq Leghari has usurped the powers of the parliament, the prime minister and cabinet by adopting unconstitutional way to announce a "relief package".
- Pakistan and India have informally agreed to resolve "minor issues relating to humanitarian matters" including release of each other's detained fishermen.
- The second phase of election 1997 has started all over the country with the scrutiny of 10,566 nomination papers filed for 217 national and 483 for four provincial assemblies seats.
DAWN
- All the five major commercial banks have stopped providing credit money to their clients after a stern warning from the State (central) Bank of Pakistan on breach of 30 percent liquidity ratio.

- Pakistan has drawn world attention to a likely threat of ballistic missile race in South Asia because of the deployment of Prithvi missile by India and warned that Pakistan reserves its right to take necessary steps to counter the Indian threat.
- A court in Karachi has remanded Asif Ali Zardsari, former investment minister and spouse of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, to judicial custody till January 2.

- The President has promulgated an ordinance to empower the Pakistan Banking Council and the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to publish a list of loan defaulters when asked by the federal government.
- The Export Import Bank of Japan and Pakistan have signed the second private sector energy development project for $140 million.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has said the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) of Benazir Bhutto has been hijacked by vested interests.
- The caretaker government has decided to arrest and prosecute 20 PPP and Pakistan Muslim League second-tier leaders under the accountability ordinance.

- Pakistani and Indian foreign ministers, at their informal meeting in New Delhi on December 18 "appeared to have accepted that it would be useful to initiate bilateral talks" between the two sides, which have remained virtually frozen for the last several years.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Sindh province's former chief minister Abdullah Shah's nomination papers for general elections due on February 3 have been rejected on various reasons at Dadu.
FINANCIAL POST
- President Farooq Leghari has announced establishment of a two billion-rupee Pakistan poverty alleviation fund for income generation and improvement in the quality of life.
- One out of 130 persons pays tax in Pakistan, says President Leghari.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
